mathematical_explanation: The proof correctly verifies the two-sided ideal criterion. The kernel is nonempty because it contains 0_R, and closure under subtraction makes it an additive subgroup. For every r in R and x in ker(phi), multiplicativity gives phi(rx) = phi(r)phi(x) = 0 and phi(xr) = phi(x)phi(r) = 0, establishing closure under multiplication from both sides even when R is noncommutative.
